Physiological anticoagulants, protein C/S pathways, antithrombin III, and fibrinolytic system regulation
ABO and Rhesus blood group systems, agglutinogens, agglutinins, and blood transfusion reactions

Microtomy: rotary microtome operation, knife types, sectioning thickness, and section mounting

Special stains: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), Masson's trichrome, Verhoeff-Van Gieson, and silver impregnation
Advanced light microscopy: polarizing microscopy, phase-contrast microscopy, and dark-field microscopy principles
Interference and ultraviolet/fluorescence microscopy principles and biological applications
Basic physical principles of diagnostic radiological imaging and plain X-ray beam generation
Radio-opacity and radiolucency densities: air, fat, water/soft tissue, bone, and contrast agents
Normal radiological anatomy of major skeletal regions, chest, and plain abdominal radiographs
Introduction to modern cross-sectional imaging: computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
Radiation biology fundamentals, radiological hazards, and occupational and patient safety measures
Physiologic anatomy of the gastrointestinal tract and enteric nervous system (myenteric and submucosal plexuses)
Electrical activity of GI smooth muscle: slow waves, interstitial cells of Cajal, and spike potentials
Gastrointestinal endocrine control: physiological actions of gastrin, CCK, secretin, GIP, and motilin
Mastication, salivary glands functional organization, salivary secretion phases, and deglutition stages
Gastric motility: receptive relaxation, gastric pump contractions, retropulsion, and gastric emptying control
Gastric secretions: hydrochloric acid biosynthesis by parietal cells, pepsinogen activation, and intrinsic factor
Regulation of gastric secretion: cephalic, gastric, and intestinal phases, and mucosal protection mechanisms
Exocrine pancreatic secretion: aqueous bicarbonate vs enzyme components, and secretin/CCK regulation
Liver and biliary physiology: bile formation, bile acid synthesis, enterohepatic circulation, and gallbladder motility
Motility of the small intestine (segmentation and peristalsis) and migrating motor complex (MMC)
Colonic motility, haustral churning, mass movements, and autonomic regulation of the defecation reflex
Digestion and intestinal absorption of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, water, electrolytes, and vitamins
General principles of hormone classification, transport, hormone-receptor interactions, and feedback loops
Cellular mechanisms of hormone action: cAMP, IP3/DAG, receptor tyrosine kinases, and nuclear receptors
Hypothalamo-pituitary axis: neurovascular portal system, hypothalamic releasing hormones, and feedback controls
Anterior pituitary hormones: growth hormone physiology, somatomedins (IGF-1), and prolactin actions
Posterior pituitary hormones: antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) and oxytocin actions and reflexes
Thyroid gland: iodide uptake, thyroglobulin iodination, T3/T4 metabolic effects, and hypothalamic-pituitary control
Adrenal cortex physiology: zona glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis hormones, and RAAS/ACTH regulation
Calcium and phosphate homeostasis: parathyroid hormone, calcitonin, and 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (Vitamin D3)
Endocrine pancreas: insulin and glucagon biosynthesis, metabolic effects, and glucose counter-regulatory mechanisms
Male reproduction: testicular Leydig and Sertoli cell functions, spermatogenesis, semen analysis, and testosterone
Female reproduction: oogenesis, ovarian and uterine menstrual cycles, ovulation surge, and estrogen/progesterone
Physiology of pregnancy, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), parturition, lactation, and contraception methods
Cellular adaptations to injury and stress: hypertrophy, hyperplasia, atrophy, and metaplasia mechanisms
Mechanisms of cell injury: free radical-mediated damage, hypoxia/ischemia, necrosis, and apoptosis cascades
Pathophysiology of red cell disorders: nutritional deficiency anaemias, aplastic anaemia, and sickle cell crises
Pathophysiology of haemostasis: thrombocytopenic purpuras, coagulopathies, and disseminated intravascular coagulation
Cardiovascular pathophysiology: cardiac arrhythmias, heart block types, and electrophysiological ectopic foci
Pathophysiology of ischemic heart disease: angina pectoris, coronary occlusion, and myocardial infarction
Pathophysiology of congestive heart failure: forward and backward failure and compensatory mechanisms
Pathophysiology of systemic arterial hypertension, hypertensive crisis, and circulatory shock stages
Pathophysiology of pulmonary diseases: obstructive (asthma, COPD) vs restrictive disorders, and FEV1/FVC ratios
Pathophysiology of pulmonary edema, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and cyanosis types
Renal pathophysiology: nephritic syndrome vs nephrotic syndrome, proteinuria, and glomerular injury
Pathophysiology of acute kidney injury (prerenal, intrarenal, postrenal) and chronic renal failure
Principles and calibration of physiological bio-amplifiers, transducers, and digital data acquisition systems
Recording and interpretation of standard 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG) and vector analysis
Arterial blood pressure monitoring: indirect auscultatory sphygmomanometry and oscillometric techniques
Pulmonary function instrumentation: spirometry calibration, spirograms, and vitalograph interpretation
Electrophysiological recording equipment: electromyography (EMG), nerve conduction studies, and oscilloscope use
Hematological diagnostic techniques: hemocytometer counting, microhematocrit centrifugation, and spectrophotometry
Principles of clinical urinalysis: dipstick chemistry, urine specific gravity, and urine sediment microscopy
In vitro organ bath systems: isolated smooth and cardiac muscle preparations and dose-response pharmacology
Laboratory safety standards, handling of biological specimens, and chemical hazard containment
Design and pedagogical execution of physiological laboratory demonstrations for medical education
Statistical analysis and error evaluation of physiological experimental data and biophysical measurements
Maintenance, troubleshooting, and quality control of physiological laboratory diagnostic devices
Functional neuroanatomy and embryological organization of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal system
Hypothalamic hypophyseotropic releasing and inhibiting hormones: TRH, CRH, GnRH, GHRH, somatostatin, and dopamine
Architecture of the hypophyseal portal microcirculation and short/long-loop servomechanism feedback systems
Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei: synthesis, neurophysin transport, and secretion of ADH and oxytocin
Neuroendocrine control of growth, metabolic development, and the hypothalamic-pituitary-somatotropic axis
Neuroendocrine regulation of reproduction: pulsatile GnRH secretion, luteinizing hormone surge, and feedback loops
The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis: diurnal ACTH circadian rhythm and neuroendocrine stress responses
Pineal gland physiology, melatonin biosynthesis from serotonin, and circadian rhythm entrainment via suprachiasmatic nucleus
Neuroendocrine regulation of energy intake, appetite control: leptin, ghrelin, NPY, and POMC pathways
Endogenous opioid peptides (endorphins, enkephalins) and their neuroendocrine modulating functions
Neuroendocrine disorders: diabetes insipidus, SIADH, hyperprolactinemia, and pituitary adenoma endocrinopathies
Autonomic-endocrine interactions in metabolic homeostasis and emergency neuroendocrine stress responses
Pathophysiology of gastrointestinal motility: achalasia cardia, dysphagia, paralytic ileus, and bowel obstruction
Pathophysiology of peptic ulcer disease: Helicobacter pylori pathogenesis, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and mucosal erosion
Pathophysiology of vomiting, diarrhea, malabsorption syndromes, and inflammatory bowel diseases
Hepatobiliary pathophysiology: hepatic failure, portal hypertension, ascites, and classification of jaundices
Pathophysiology of the anterior pituitary: gigantism, acromegaly, pituitary dwarfism, and hypopituitarism
Pathophysiology of thyroid gland: Graves' hyperthyroidism, thyrotoxicosis, endemic goitre, cretinism, and myxedema
Pathophysiology of adrenal cortex: Cushing's syndrome, Addison's disease, and primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's)
Pathophysiology of diabetes mellitus: Type 1 vs Type 2 pathogenesis, diabetic ketoacidosis, and chronic angiopathies
Disorders of the motor nervous system: upper vs lower motor neuron lesions, and ALS pathophysiology
Basal ganglia disorders: Parkinson's disease, Huntington's chorea, hemiballismus, and involuntary movement disorders
Pathophysiology of sensory disturbances: tabes dorsalis, syringomyelia, thalamic pain syndrome, and brown-sequard
Pathophysiology of epilepsy, seizure classifications, demyelinating disease (multiple sclerosis), and myasthenia gravis

courses.canonical_name: Metabolism of Nucleic Acid and Protein Synthesis
aliases: Nucleic Acid Metabolism and Protein Synthesis
core_topics: De novo purine nucleotide biosynthesis: PRPP synthetase, 10-step synthesis of IMP, and reciprocal AMP/GMP regulation
Purine salvage pathway: HGPRT and APRT reactions, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, and gout pathophysiology
Purine catabolism: xanthine oxidase mechanism, uric acid generation, hyperuricemia, and allopurinol action
Pyrimidine nucleotide synthesis: CAD complex, UMP synthesis, CTP production, and orotic acidurias
Deoxyribonucleotide synthesis: ribonucleotide reductase regulation, and thymidylate synthase inhibition by 5-fluorouracil
DNA replication enzymology in prokaryotes and eukaryotes: DNA polymerases, helicases, topoisomerases, and telomerase
Mechanisms of DNA repair: nucleotide excision repair, base excision repair, and mismatch repair defects
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic transcription: RNA polymerases, promoters, enhancers, and transcription factors
Post-transcriptional modifications: 5'-capping, 3'-polyadenylation, and spliceosome-mediated intron splicing
The genetic code: non-overlapping, degenerate, universal triplets, start/stop codons, and wobble hypothesis
Amino acid activation, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and ribosomal assembly (initiation, elongation, termination)
Post-translational modifications of nascent proteins, protein targeting, and antibiotic inhibitors of translation
Mechanisms of metabolic regulation: enzyme compartmentalization, allosteric control, and covalent phosphorylation
Major metabolic crossroads: metabolic fates of glucose-6-phosphate, pyruvate, and acetyl-CoA
Organ-specific metabolic specializations: liver, skeletal muscle, heart, brain, and adipose tissue
The well-fed (absorptive) state: postprandial insulin surges, glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis
The fasting (post-absorptive) state: glucagon elevation, hepatic glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, and lipolysis
Metabolic adaptations during prolonged starvation: ketone body adaptation by the brain and muscle protein sparing
Hormonal coordination of fuel metabolism: reciprocal actions of insulin, glucagon, epinephrine, and cortisol
Inter-organ metabolic cycles: the Cori cycle, glucose-alanine cycle, and Randle (glucose-fatty acid) cycle
Metabolic derangements in Diabetes Mellitus: ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar states, and dyslipidemia
Role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) as a central cellular sensor of energy balance
Ethanol metabolism: alcohol dehydrogenase, MEOS pathway, elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio, and metabolic consequences
Biochemical basis of metabolic syndrome: insulin resistance, ectopic lipid deposition, and systemic lipotoxicity
Nutritional energy requirements: Caloric value of food, Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), and Specific Dynamic Action (SDA)
Dietary carbohydrate, fat, and protein requirements, nitrogen balance (positive vs negative), and essential nutrients
Protein-energy malnutrition (PEM): biochemical lesions, pathophysiology, and clinical features of Kwashiorkor and Marasmus
Fat-soluble vitamins: structure, absorption, transport, biochemical functions, and deficiency/toxicity of Vitamins A, D, E, and K
Water-soluble B-complex vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7): active coenzymes, biochemical pathways, and deficiencies
Folate and Vitamin B12: one-carbon unit transfers, homocysteine methylation, methyl trap, and megaloblastic anaemia
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid): collagen hydroxylation, antioxidant properties, and clinical manifestations of scurvy
Mineral metabolism: sodium, potassium, and chloride distributions, fluid balance, and water intake-output regulation
Calcium and phosphorus metabolism: intestinal absorption, bone remodeling, and hormonal regulation by PTH and calcitriol
Trace elements: iron absorption, transferrin, ferritin, iron deficiency anaemia, and hemochromatosis
Trace minerals: zinc, copper (Wilson's and Menkes diseases), selenium, iodine, and trace element deficiencies
Dietary fiber and antioxidant nutrients in the prevention of cardiovascular disease and metabolic disorders
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic gene structure: promoters, operons (lac operon), introns, exons, and regulatory elements
Regulation of eukaryotic gene expression: chromatin remodeling, histone acetylation/methylation, and transcription factors
Molecular basis of gene mutations: missense, nonsense, frameshift, splice-site mutations, and phenotypic effects
Molecular pathology of hemoglobinopathies: sickle cell anemia (HbS point mutation) and alpha/beta thalassemias
Recombinant DNA technology: restriction endonucleases, DNA ligases, and cloning vectors (plasmids, phages, BACs)
Generation of genomic and complementary DNA (cDNA) libraries, and screening by hybridization
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR): reaction mechanics, primer design, RT-PCR, quantitative real-time PCR, and diagnostic uses
Molecular blotting techniques: Southern blotting (DNA), Northern blotting (RNA), and Western blotting (proteins)
DNA sequencing methodologies: Sanger dideoxy method, automated fluorescence sequencing, and Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)
Recombinant protein expression: therapeutic production of human insulin, growth hormone, and monoclonal antibodies
Principles of gene therapy: viral/non-viral vectors, ex vivo vs in vivo approaches, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
Personalized medicine: pharmacogenomics, genetic polymorphic variations, and individual therapeutic optimization

courses.system_region: Special Topics and Applied Medical Biochemistry
core_topics: Hormone biochemistry: chemical classes, biosynthesis, and second messenger signalling mechanisms (cAMP, IP3, DAG, tyrosine kinase)
Metabolism of xenobiotics: Phase I functionalization (Cytochrome P450 isozymes) and Phase II conjugation reactions
Detoxification pathways, microsomal enzyme induction, inhibition, and mechanisms of biochemical drug resistance
Forensic biochemistry: DNA profiling, short tandem repeats (STRs), medico-legal fluid, blood, and sweat analysis
Biochemistry of aging and cellular senescence: telomere shortening, cumulative oxidative damage, and advanced glycation products
Biochemical mechanisms of apoptosis: intrinsic (mitochondrial/cytochrome c) and extrinsic (death receptor) pathways
Neurobiochemistry: neurotransmitters (acetylcholine, dopamine, GABA, glutamate) biosynthesis, degradation, and receptors
Biochemistry of muscle contraction: actomyosin ATP cross-bridge cycle and metabolic pathways during intense exercise
Heme biosynthesis pathway, control by ALA synthase, porphyrias, and bilirubin metabolism and hyperbilirubinemias
Molecular biochemistry of oncogenesis: proto-oncogenes, viral oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes (TP53, RB1), and apoptosis evasion
Biochemical features of viral infections: retroviral reverse transcriptase, HIV replication cycle, and antiviral targets
Molecular genetics of Burkitt's lymphoma: c-myc translocation, chromosome 8:14 rearrangement, and metabolic features of tropical diseases
